exposure: colostrum volume fed at first meal
time to first feeding (delay between birth and first colostrum meal)
outcome: adequate transfer of passive immunity (TPI; defined as serum Brix refractance >=8.4%)
cohort: A total of 818 calves from 61 commercial Holstein dairy farms were included in this study.
finding: Calves receiving >=2.5 L colostrum at their first meal, colostrum with >=24.5% Brix, or colostrum within 3 hours after birth had significantly higher odds of adequate transfer of passive immunity, while bacterial contamination was not associated.
